The docket design's own recount instruction: "the implementer MUST re-count the actual table-driven test-case total by direct inspection ... rather than trust the heuristic figure at face value" -- the ~2,969 figure (rules/\* ~2,222 + engine ~747) is NOT the denominator used below. This converter's own recount, by direct AST inspection (see package doc comment for the exact two idioms recognised), is:

- Files scanned: 79
- Recognised tables (idiom A batches + idiom B struct tables): 438
- Denominator (elements across every recognised table): 3324
- Extracted (converted to a corpus row): 2859
- Unconvertible rows (recognised table, element not statically resolvable): 465
- **Ratio: 0.8601** (exit bar: >= 0.95)

**Below the 95% exit bar.** Per the docket design's own acceptance criterion ("or the shortfall is explicitly listed as remainder"), the remainder is listed below rather than force-converting it.

## Manual-disposition-per-family carve-out (fakes/stubs, tempdir state)

Docket design, Phase 0 item 3 (verbatim): "Rows depending on rule-level fakes/stubs (10 of 57 rules/* test files define fakes; 14 build tempdir state) are dispositioned manually per family." This converter's own recount, via the packet's own mechanical hint (`type [Ff]ake|type .*Stub\b`/`t.TempDir\(\)|ioutil.TempDir`):

- Files matching a fake/stub type declaration: 3
- Files matching tempdir construction: 17

Note: the tempdir count matches the design's cited "14" exactly (counting `internal/rules/*` only; this report's totals above also include `internal/engine`, hence the slightly higher raw numbers). The fake/stub count does NOT match the design's cited "10" -- several patterns were tried (`type [Ff]ake\w*|type \w*Stub\b`, a looser `type \w*([Ff]ake|Stub)\w*`, a bare case-insensitive `fake` substring, `httptest.NewServer`) and the highest count found across `internal/rules/*` alone was 4 files (envvars, kubectl, killshell, buildtools), not 10 -- the same "do not trust the heuristic figure at face value" caution the packet applies to the ~2,969 row estimate evidently also applies to this count; this section reports the actual pattern-matched files rather than force-matching the cited total.

These files' tables ARE still attempted by the same two idioms above (a file can have some mechanically-extractable rows and still need per-family manual disposition for its fake/stub-dependent cases) -- listed here for the manual reviewer, grouped by family:

## Legacy-vs-new disagreements (acceptance criterion: each resolved into one of three buckets)

Every extracted Bash/Write/Edit/MultiEdit row was run through the SAME production `claudecodeadapter.Evaluate` chain (`cmddesc.DefaultRegistry()`, `effectpolicy.DefaultPolicies()`, `effectpolicy.DefaultGraphPolicies()`) with a zero-value `RequestConfig` (matching the row's own empty Settings/RulesConfig fixture), and compared against the row's own (legacy) expected_verdict.

- Comparable (Bash or a file-edit tool the adapter models): 2787
- Not comparable (adapter has no opinion on this tool, or refused the input outright): 72
- Agreed: 1193
- Disagreed: 1594

Disposition breakdown:

- new too strict: 1241
- comparison artifact (not a genuine disagreement): 168
- needs manual review: 185

**Methodology and its limitations** (read before trusting the "new too strict" and "comparison artifact" buckets below):

- `accepted change`: same restrictiveness rank (Approve < NotApprove < Reject), different verdict spelling. Structurally cannot fire today, since both old and new verdicts are already mapped into the corpus's own 3-value Verdict before comparison (a rank tie implies verdict equality) -- kept for a future engine whose comparison space is richer than 3 values.
- `comparison artifact (not a genuine disagreement)`: the new engine's reason cites operator configuration (vetted hosts, kube contexts, remote paths) this comparison pass never populates (RequestConfig is zero-value, matching every row's own empty RulesConfig fixture). These are NOT resolved into one of the three named buckets -- they are a known limitation of running this comparison unconfigured, not a legacy-vs-new policy finding.
- `new too strict` (spec/policy work): the new engine's reason cites a registry/policy COVERAGE gap -- no cmddesc schema for the command, an unmodeled subcommand/operand/flag, an assignment-only expression with "no executable" to judge, or an entire command approved outright ("all N command nodes permitted") because the specific family's policy (primarycommit/primarypush/gitdir-write-protection/etc.) has not been ported into `effectpolicy.DefaultPolicies` yet. R1 states the effect engine REPLACES RuleChain, but the per-family RETARGET (porting each rule family's domain knowledge into cmddesc schemas and effectpolicy policies) is explicitly later-phase work, not this packet's -- so this bucket is used for BOTH symptom directions (the new engine looking too strict on an unmodeled tool, or too permissive on a not-yet-ported policy), because the root cause and the remedy (add the missing schema/policy) are identical either way. A reviewer relying on verdict direction alone should read each row's own Rationale, which always states the literal old/new verdicts.
- `needs manual review`: a genuine strictness delta with no mechanically-diagnosable cause -- resolve into "old was a hole" vs "new too strict" by reading the actual command.
